              items:

              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's display name, formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: Franklin, George
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The owner's initials, formatted as upper-cased first letters
                of the first and last name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: G.F.
              readOnly: true
            registrationDate:
              title: Registration date
              description: The date the pet owner was registered. Defaults to the
                current date when not supplied.
              type: string
              format: date
              example: '2010-09-07'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: The owner's sequential membership number, assigned on
                creation as one more than the number of owners at that time.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              example: 11
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, assigned on creation and
                formatted as '<UPPERCASE_CITY>-<NNNN>' where NNNN is one more than
                the number of owners already in that city, zero-padded to four digits.
              type: string
              example: LONDON-0007
              readOnly: true
            membershipTier:
              title: Membership tier
              description: The owner's membership tier, assigned on creation. The
                first 100 owners ever created are 'FOUNDING'; all later owners are
                'STANDARD'.
              type: string
              example: FOUNDING
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of other owners that already shared this
                owner's last name at the moment it was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            sharesHousehold:
              title: Shares household
              description: Whether, at the moment this owner was created, another
                owner already had the same address and city.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object

## Summary

I implemented the `locality` field on owner creation following the codebase's established pattern for computed owner fields (like `namesakeCount` and `sharesHousehold`).

**The rule:** on `POST /api/owners`, a new owner's `locality` is `"local"` if the owner's city is the *single* most common city among owners that already exist at that moment, otherwise `"remote"`. A tie for most common city means there is no single most common city, so `"remote"`. The owner being created isn't yet saved, so it's never counted against itself. Cities are compared case-insensitively.

**Changes:**
- **`AssignOwnerLocality.java`** (new) — computes the locality from `ownerRepository.findAll()` before save, mirroring the existing `AssignOwner*` functions.
- **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired `assignLocality` into the pipeline between `assignSharesHousehold` and `save`, under the same `transaction` governance.
- **`Owner.java`** — added the `locality` field (`@Column(name = "locality")`) with getter/setter.
- **`openapi.yml`** — added the `locality` property to the `Owner` schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct maps it by name).
- **schema.sql** for all four databases (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) — added the `locality VARCHAR(20)` column.

The provided `Cp18Tests` passes, and no existing tests regressed.
